Paragraph1: "Oregon’s pioneering decriminalization effort, which made possession of small amounts of hard drugs a civil violation, will end on Sunday when a new statute takes effect. The law, known as HB4002, returns such possession to criminal status but offers an alternative route to treatment instead of immediate arrest."

Paragraph2: "Under the new rule, anyone found with substances like fentanyl, heroin or meth can either face a misdemeanor charge punishable by up to six months in jail or opt for a treatment pathway that requires completing a behavioral health program and joining a deflection initiative. Paragraph3: "While the statute encourages counties to establish local treatment alternatives that divert people from jail toward health services, it does not require them to do so.
